I have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I know every plot. My household has nine people, but the younger ones work in factories or construction in the city, so it is mainly my wife and me handling the day-to-day work, with the family coming back for harvest. I have a well, so water is reliable, but I do not waste it — electricity for the pump costs money.

My land is split into two blocks. About six mu goes into wheat-maize double cropping — this is my staple system. The remaining four mu I plant to cotton. Wheat is already in the ground from last October; now is green-up season. I will topdress it with urea and give it the first spring irrigation soon. I use improved wheat seed — I buy fresh seed every few years to keep vigor, but I do not need the most expensive hybrids for wheat. Before sowing wheat I always rotary till to get a fine seedbed. I apply basal compound fertilizer at sowing, then urea at green-up and jointing. I expect about 525 jin per mu from wheat if the weather holds.

For summer maize, I plant directly into the wheat stubble without ploughing — no-tillage saves me precious days between wheat harvest in early June and maize sowing. Time is short then, and everyone in the village does it this way now. I buy hybrid maize seed, usually something like Denghai, because the yield gain pays for the seed cost. Maize does not need much extra nitrogen if the wheat was fertilized well — maybe a small side-dressing of urea at jointing. I irrigate twice, at the jointing and grain-filling stages. I expect around 625 jin per mu.

Cotton is different — it needs more labor, especially spraying. Bollworms and aphids are the enemy, so I spray about fifteen times from June to August. I rotary till the cotton field in spring before planting. I use improved cotton varieties. Cotton gets a small amount of compound fertilizer at planting, and I irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. Yield should be around 280 jin per mu. Cotton prices have been acceptable, and the income helps with household expenses.

This is the plan I follow every year. It is not fancy, but forty years of experience tells me it works on this soil.
